title: Rec.Truncate in AL
summary: Rec.Truncate is a new AL method based on SQL Server TRUNCATE TABLE that empties a table in milliseconds rather than deleting row by row. If a constraint is hit (system or virtual table, try function, security filters, delete event subscribers, Media fields, many marked rows, FlowField filters) it falls back to slow DeleteAll behavior. With filters it saves rows to keep and restores them, which only pays off when removing about 50-60% or more.
key_points: Truncating a whole table without filters is far faster than DeleteAll, and the gap grows with more records, indexes and SIFTs

Listed constraints such as active security filters, OnBeforeDelete/OnAfterDelete subscribers, Media fields, try functions, many marked rows or FlowField filters make it fall back to row-by-row deletion
Filtered truncate copies rows to keep into a temp table, disables SIFTs, truncates, then restores rows and rebuilds indexes; deleting a small slice was dramatically slower than DeleteAll in the demo
Lab tests on a one million row Item Ledger Entry clone showed truncate pays off only when deleting at least 50-60% of a table with few indexes
Best suited to staging and log tables that are emptied completely; test all scenarios before relying on it

quotes.text: when cleaning a table with few indexes, the truncate method becomes advantageous if deleting at least 50% - 60% of the content
quotes.why_it_matters: Provides the critical threshold at which truncate outperforms DeleteAll, essential for deciding which method to use

quotes.text: If filtered, check the number of records to be deleted and decide what to do.
quotes.why_it_matters: Highlights that truncate with filters requires careful analysis because it can become slower than DeleteAll when deleting small portions
